title: Stakeholder activation timeline and telemetry contract (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a proposed cross-functional activation timeline and a minimal telemetry contract for canary and A/B experiments for the Console + Rollouts product area. The goal is a pragmatic, checklist-oriented artifact teams can use to coordinate launches with the SRE, Observability, Product, and Solutions teams.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to incremental feature rollouts that affect model routing, traffic-slicing, or inference configuration (batching, quantization, KV cache behavior).
- Does NOT replace deeper security/compliance reviews required for Private deployments.
- Assumes teams will run at least one synthetic traffic sweep before public exposure.

High-level objectives:
1) Align stakeholders on when to expect signals, who owns each signal, and what thresholds gate progression.
2) Define a small, actionable telemetry contract (metric names, tags, sampling, alert rules).
3) Reduce friction for rapid rollback or automated fallback when canary signals exceed risk thresholds.

Stakeholders (roles, not people):
- Product owner (feature hypothesis, business criteria) -> ensures hypothesis and primary success metric defined.
- Experiment steward (product/pm) -> runs the activation timeline and notes.
- Observability lead (metrics, sampling, dashboards) -> implements telemetry contract and dashboards.
- SRE/Infra (latency, capacity, error budgets) -> monitors infra-level SLOs and assists with scaling rules.
- Applied ML / ModelOps (model-level regressions, hallucination checks) -> provides QA sets and model-run baselines.
- Solutions/CS (customer-impact triage) -> on-call for customer escalations during exposure window.

Activation timeline (template to adapt per launch):
- T-minus 7 days: Feature-complete PR, run unit/regression tests. Notify stakeholders and add to weekly rollout sync.
- T-minus 5 days: Observability lead adds baseline panels for required metrics; synthetic generator script prepared (see linked_artifacts).
- T-minus 3 days: Run full synthetic traffic sweep (10k requests, varied input length). Log KV cache hits/misses, model variant fallbacks.
- T-minus 2 days: Canary configuration uploaded to environment, 0.5% internal traffic only. Start 6-hour observation window.
- T-minus 1 day: Broaden to 2% internal + trusted customers (opt-in). Run automated evaluation set against model outputs for quality regressions.
- Day 0: Activate canary at 5% external traffic if all gate checks green. Continue 24–72 hour observation depending on severity.
- Day 3+: Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with at least 24 hours between steps, or faster with explicit stakeholder approval.

Telemetry contract (minimal required metrics):
- metric: rwi.inference.request_count | tags: [env, route, model_version, cohort] | description: total requests handled.
- metric: rwi.inference.latency.p50/p90/p99_ms | tags: [env, route, model_version, cohort] | description: end-to-end latency in ms.
- metric: rwi.inference.token_rate | tags: [env, route, model_version] | description: tokens/sec produced (useful to identify throughput regressions).
- metric: rwi.inference.errors.count | tags: [env, route, model_version, error_type] | description: 4xx/5xx and inference-specific errors (OOM, KV-miss-error).
- metric: rwi.inference.fallbacks.count | tags: [env, route, model_version, fallback_target] | description: number of requests routed to fallback model/variant.
- metric: rwi.inference.kv_cache.hit_ratio | tags: [env, model_version] | description: prefix/KV cache hit ratio over window.
- metric: rwi.quality.regression.score_delta | tags: [eval_set, model_version] | description: delta in automated quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim) vs baseline.
- logs: request_id, route, model_version, cohort, latency_ms, tokens_output, fallback (boolean), kv_cache_hit (boolean) — minimum fields required in structured logs for sampling.

Tagging conventions (critical for slicing):
- env: {dev, staging, prod}
- route: stable string path for API route
- model_version: semantic version or commit tag
- cohort: can be {control, canary, cohortA, cohortB, internal} — must be present for any experimental exposure

Sampling guidance:
- Full sampling for canary cohorts (100% of canary traffic).
- 10% sampling of control production requests to compare distributions in near-real time. Use randomized hash on request_id to ensure stable sampling slice per user where relevant.

Gating rules (stop / rollback conditions):
- Immediate rollback: any increase in rwi.inference.errors.count > 5x baseline sustained for 5 minutes AND concurrent spike in p99 latency > 2x baseline.
- Soft stop / hold progression: quality regression score_delta drops below -0.02 relative to baseline on the canonical eval set OR KV cache hit_ratio drops > 15% leading to latency regressions.
- Manual review: any customer-visible hallucination or safety incident flagged by Solutions or Security.

Alerting and dashboards (observability lead responsibilities):
- Create a canary dashboard that aggregates the telemetry contract by cohort and model_version. Panels: request_count, p99 latency over time, error rate, fallback count, quality_score_delta, kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Pager thresholds: if rwi.inference.errors.count > threshold for 5 min -> page SRE.
- Pager only on infra-level SLO breaches or safety incidents. Product and ML get Slack alerts for quality regressions.

Experiment analytics (A/B):
- Define primary metric at hypothesis time (e.g., rerank CTR change, latency at p95 cost tradeoff). Secondary metrics listed in telemetry contract.
- Use deterministic assignment key (user_id or session hashed) and log cohort assignment in structured logs.
- Ensure experimentization middleware emits cohort tag to metrics backend and interactive dashboards.
- Plan uplift window and statistical test (e.g., two-sided t-test or bootstrap CI) and the minimum detectable effect (MDE). Record these in the rollout ticket.

Operational runbook snippet (quick actions):
- If canary error spikes: 1) Pause traffic routing, 2) Switch canary cohort to fallback model (automated policy if configured), 3) Notify product + SRE + ML, 4) Collect top 20 failing request ids and a sanitized payload snapshot.
- If quality regression without infra impact: 1) Pause ramp, 2) Initiate model-eval review with ML, 3) Consider targeted rollback for affected cohorts.

Open questions / decision items (to resolve before T-minus 3):
- Do we require production-sampled control traffic to be stored for 48 hours for replay? cost implications vs. debug agility.
- Should canary cohorts inherit quota limits of the control path or have temporary elevated quotas for meaningful signal? (SRE to advise).
- Default MDE for conversational quality experiments (PM/ML to propose).

Next steps (owner: Rohit Kapoor):
- [ ] Sync with Observability lead (Evelyn) to finalize metric names and dashboard template — target: 2025-02-18.
- [ ] Add gating thresholds to rollout ticket RK-2143 and include synthetic sweep script outputs — target: 2025-02-20.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing comms template for opt-in canaries and post-mortem skeleton — target: 2025-02-24.

Notes to self / working assumptions:
- This is deliberately lightweight: primary aim is to ensure consistent instrumentation and quick, unambiguous decisions during rollouts.
- We rely on the existing fallback policy engine (infra) to perform instant model swaps; if not available, we must add an emergency playbook for DNS/traffic routing.
